lead_headline: Dispatch completes its full stack in a single day; Claude Code runs a mass triage
lead_body: Nine commits took Dispatch from skeleton to deployable: Phases 2–7 landed together, followed by a configurable scheduler, a manual trigger, a backfill script, and an architectural note pinning Caddy as the gateway. Claude Code's tracker saw a bulk closure of roughly fifty issues around 22:35, with new reports arriving through the night on MCP respawn failures, credential detection, and a word-boundary fix for the @claude trigger.
lead_article:
Dispatch dominated the day. Nine commits landed across the full stack — Phases 2 through 7 in a single push brought the Vite SPA, encrypted settings, admin APIs, and pluggable storage into place, followed by a deploy configuration for revamp-dispatch.marklab.uk and a discreet admin gear icon tucked beside the brand mark. The afternoon and evening filled in the remaining surfaces: configurable generation time with timezone-aware UI, a manual briefing trigger with idempotent lead and addendum handling, a backfill and bootstrap script, and a commit clarifying Caddy's role as the gateway. That last one is architectural prose, not code — worth having in the repo regardless.

Claude Code had a characteristically loud day in the tracker: a mass closure of roughly fifty issues around 22:35 points to a triage pass, while new reports continued arriving through the night — MCP stdio servers not respawning after plugin autoupdates, a credential-guard plugin PR adding hardcoded secret detection, a word-boundary fix for the @claude trigger to stop it firing on @claude-* variants, and a CLI-desktop conversation sync proposal. Astro contributed a single tight PR caching resolved actions in the base pipeline. The Hydrogen deploy flag conflict — --env and --env-branch being mutually exclusive without documentation — surfaced as a user-filed bug, nothing requiring immediate action.
